column1: # Drugged nodes of the mitotic machinery: the gene set behind the report's "drugged neighbourhood"
# statement in the therapeutic-problem section.
# WHAT THIS FILE IS AND IS NOT. The gene set is curated: these are the mitotic-machinery proteins
# with the best-known drug discovery programmes, chosen because the question is "what do the drugs
# near this pathway do", not "which genes are near BUB1B". It is not a computed neighbourhood and
# the report does not claim it is exhaustive. What IS computed, at run time against the Open Targets
# release recorded in the provenance, is the evidence: every clinical candidate against each gene,
# its mechanism action type, and whether the gene carries one of the mitotic-fidelity GO terms the
# anti-target rule uses. Nothing in the report asserts a drug's direction from this file.
# A gene with no clinical candidate stays in the set. The point of the statement is the direction of
# the drugs that exist, and a gene the field has not drugged is part of that picture.
# ensembl_id is resolved from the symbol by ot_query.py at run time; the column here is the expected
# value, checked against what the API returns so a symbol change is caught rather than absorbed.
